subject: Business Models
title: Membership Models
description: A fast breakdown of Membership Models for builders.

hook.text: Amazon Prime has 200 million members paying $139/year. That's $28 billion before selling a single product.

buildup.text: Memberships lock in spending. Prime members spend $1,400/year on Amazon vs $600 for non-members.

discovery.text: The psychology: once you've paid the fee, you feel compelled to 'get your money's worth' by using it more.

twist.text: Costco makes almost all its profit from membership fees, not product sales. The store is a perk.

climax.text: Memberships create loyalty moats. Switching means losing perceived value you've already paid for.

punchline.text: Pay to enter, then spend more. Memberships are brilliant traps.

quiz.question: Where does Costco make almost all its profit?

details.summary: Membership models charge recurring fees for access to exclusive benefits, content, or community rather than specific products. Costco charges annual fees for warehouse access, Amazon Prime bundles shipping and streaming, and professional associations provide networking and credentials.
details.whyItMatters: Memberships create predictable revenue, high retention, and emotional loyalty that transaction-based models cannot match. The psychology of belonging makes members more engaged and less price-sensitive to incremental purchases within the ecosystem.
takeaways: Recurring fees grant access to exclusive benefits and community
Membership creates psychological commitment beyond transactional loyalty
Retention rates for well-designed memberships exceed 90% annually

faq.question: What makes Costco's membership model so effective?
faq.answer: Costco earns most of its profit from membership fees, not product margins. This lets it price products extremely low, which justifies the membership fee. Members who have paid upfront shop more frequently to maximize their investment. Renewal rates exceed 90% globally.

faq.question: How is a membership model different from a subscription?
faq.answer: Subscriptions typically provide access to a specific product or service. Memberships create a broader relationship with access to multiple benefits, community, and identity. The distinction is psychological: memberships feel like belonging while subscriptions feel like bills.
